column1: # EARLY-RETURN-FIXTURES - the fixtures a test may return early on, before it asserts anything,
# and where that road is taken (0.4.10 plan row 12, T-INSTALL-TESTS-SILENT-PASS-OFF-WINDOWS).
# crates/bt-source/tests/early_returns.rs reads every #[test] function's own body for a road
# out (`return;`, `return ();`, `return Ok(..);`). R: a road written after the test's first
# assertion is dropped, not registered here: each stands in EARLY-RETURN-DROPPED.tsv, with
# the assertion before it and a dated reason. Every other road stands in one of the shapes
# G1 the else of a `let`, G2 an `if` with no `else` (the last arm of an `else if` chain
# included), G3 a `match` arm, each judged by the callee of the
# expression it hangs on (or that expression's whole text, whitespace out, when it is no
# call). G4, the child half of a test whose expression reads only variables its own file sets
# on a started command (`.env(NAME, ..)`), needs no row. A road out in no shape is refused
# outright. The guard holds this list to the sites both ways: a site no row names is red, and
# a row that names no site is stale and red.
# test: `*` when the callee is a function named by its path (the row is keyed on the file and
# the callee, and covers every test of the file that calls it); otherwise - a method read on no
# call, a variable, a whole condition, a read of the environment G4 does not hold - the name of
# the one test function the row covers.
# hosts: exactly `other-unix` (a Unix that is not macOS), `other-platform` (neither Windows nor
# a Unix), `environment: <fact>` (a machine of any platform that lacks something),
# `parent-half` (the road is the parent's, once the test's own child process passed) or
# `child-half` (the test is a child another test starts - its mode read from the arguments,
# standard input, or a variable set under a spelling G4 cannot match: another file's command, or
# a helper's parameter as in `.env(child, ..)` - and in the suite's own run is not that child). Never Windows or macOS: every suite of the workspace runs there, and a test that
# returns early there for a platform fact is gated with #[cfg] instead (CONVENTIONS H1 rule 2).
# Where a fixture answers nothing on a whole platform all the same, the reason says so, with
# the plan row that decides it.
